analysis:
I examined the .github/workflows/ci.yml head text and the docs-impact.yml patch. The changes are CI-only: SAVE_CACHES now gates cache writes to pushes to master or dev, and a CHECKOUT_SPARSE variable skips evidence archives and landing videos.

Every checkout now restores a saved .git cache, checks out over it, and falls back to a cold checkout on failure.

The cache-poisoning angle checks out. Cache saves (lines 97, 207, 277, 522, 727, 937, 1080, 1149, 1214, and the cluster and audio cache saves) require SAVE_CACHES=='true'. That is true only for push events on master or dev, so pull-request code, including fork PRs, cannot write .git caches. Pull requests only restore caches from the base branch scope. persist-credentials:false is set on every checkout before .git is saved, so the job token is not stored in the cached .git/config. Workflow permissions remain contents: read. Actions are still pinned to SHAs. The new git-day step writes only date-derived values to GITHUB_OUTPUT, with no untrusted input interpolated into run scripts. TARGET_BRANCH is passed via env rather than inline, so there is no script injection.

The sparse-checkout and blob:none filter in docs-impact.yml (lines 61-68) only reduce what is fetched. They do not change the checked-out ref or the permissions model. The base text of that file was not supplied, so I could not confirm its event trigger or token scope. These are pre-existing and unchanged by this patch.

No provider runtime, attestation, key, or cache-storage behavior changed. The only link to T-041 is the unchanged DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0 settings in the test steps. No threat-model gap results from this PR.

Remaining question for integration: confirm docs-impact.yml does not run untrusted PR code with elevated privileges. That is pre-existing and not introduced here.
